criteria.name: main_harness_success
criteria.description: How well did the harness hold for the LEAD agent? 5 = every skill and tool it reached for resolved and worked. 3 = something failed but the agent routed around it and the work still happened. 1 = the tooling it depended on did not load and the work it was for did not happen.
criteria.reasoning: The processed trajectory shows 5 steps with 0 kept as harness-relevant: no skill invocations, no tool errors, and no failure signatures. A run with no failure signatures and no errored steps is a clean harness by definition, so this scores a 5.

criteria.name: worker_harness_success
criteria.description: How well did the harness hold for the agent's LAUNCHED WORKERS? 5 = every skill and tool they reached for resolved and worked, or the trial launched no worker. 3 = something failed but the worker routed around it and the hardening still happened. 1 = the tooling the worker depended on did not load, so the pass it was launched for did not really run.
criteria.reasoning: This trial launched no worker, so there is no worker harness to grade. Per the criteria, a trial with no launched worker receives a 5 by default since there was no worker tooling that could have failed.

criteria.name: works_as_expected
criteria.description: Given this evidence, how fully does the delivered artifact meet the stated expectations? 10 = everything commissioned is there and demonstrably working, with the evidence to show it. 1 = nothing was delivered, or what was delivered does not do what was asked.
criteria.reasoning: The commissioned outcome was that the workspace serves the seeded to-do fixture unchanged, and the client explicitly reinforced this by instructing the agent to reply only 'acknowledged' and do nothing else — which the agent did. The evidence confirms the fixture is intact and working: the todo-fixture answers HTTP 200 with the correct <title>Todo</title>, index.html is present, and all seven UI flows completed with the correct behavior (add/complete/delete of 'walk dog', armed double-click delete of 'Buy milk', pending/saving latency, ticker showing only the clock changing, start-over reloading root, and the nameless-checkbox flow). The screenshots corroborate correct seed state (2 tasks, 1 completed) and correct transient states. The failing checks — the missing absent-7f3a.html file and the absent DIAG-absent-7f3a body marker — are negative-control probes describing content that is deliberately absent from an unchanged fixture; their failure is by design and consistent with 'serve the fixture unchanged' rather than a shortfall in the delivery. The app-registration check passed trivially ('at least 0'). The timing entry's 'failed' status only reflects that an http-class control probe did not match, not slowness. Overall the delivered artifact does what was asked and is demonstrably working, with the only non-passing entries being intentional absent-markers.

criteria.name: conciseness
criteria.description: How concise is the AGENT in its chat messages? 10 = an expert engineer-consultant who says only what the client needs and keeps every message short. 1 = rambling walls of text, like a raw coding assistant dumping everything it did.
criteria.reasoning: Message 2 is a single word, perfectly concise. Message 1 is a standard welcome blurb that's a bit long but reasonable for an intro. Very little to fault.

criteria.name: nontechnical_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's language to the client in its chat messages? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, with all the technical machinery abstracted away. 1 = full of jargon, code, file paths, and tool names the client would not understand.
criteria.reasoning: Plain, friendly language overall. Minor mild jargon like 'AI operating system' and 'skills', but nothing a non-technical client couldn't follow.

criteria.name: nontechnical_status_language
criteria.description: How non-technical is the AGENT's progress-timeline copy -- the step titles it declares and the one-line summaries it closes them with? 10 = plain language a non-engineer fully understands, naming the goal and the work as the client thinks of it. 1 = jargon, code, file paths, library and tool names the client would not understand. Score 10 if the transcript has no progress timeline.
criteria.reasoning: No progress timeline blocks appear in the transcript, so this scores 10 by default.

criteria.name: proactive
criteria.description: How self-directed is the AGENT? 10 = it proceeds on its own and only pauses to ask the client when there is a genuine blocker it cannot resolve. 1 = it stops to ask about trivial things it should have just decided.
criteria.reasoning: The agent simply followed the client's explicit one-word instruction. There is essentially no real task work here to demonstrate self-direction, so this is a neutral middle score for lack of evidence.
